title: Fiscal year-to-date, quarter-to-date and month-to-date measures in DAX
summary: Reusable DAX measures for YTD, QTD and MTD sales with a configurable fiscal year end, prior-year YTD comparison, rolling 12 months and a guard that stops the lines at the last day with data.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- Creates the standard time-to-date family on top of one base measure. The fiscal year ends on 30 June in the example,
-- change the string to "12/31" for a calendar year. A guard returns blank for future periods, so line charts
-- do not run flat to the end of the Date table.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Measures use Sales[SalesAmount], Sales[OrderDate] and the Date table with Date[Date] and Date[MonthNumber].

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

-- Last day with data, ignoring every filter in the report (dates, products, customers)
Last Sales Date =
CALCULATE ( MAX ( Sales[OrderDate] ), REMOVEFILTERS () )

-- Fiscal year label for slicers and axes (fiscal year starts 1 July, named after the year in which it ends)
-- Calculated column on the Date table:
Fiscal Year =
"FY" & ( YEAR ( 'Date'[Date] ) + IF ( MONTH ( 'Date'[Date] ) > 6, 1, 0 ) )

-- Fiscal year to date; "6/30" is the fiscal year end (use "12/31" for calendar years)
Sales FYTD =
VAR LastDate = [Last Sales Date]
RETURN
    IF (
        MIN ( 'Date'[Date] ) <= LastDate,
        TOTALYTD ( [Total Sales], 'Date'[Date], "6/30" )
    )

-- Quarter and month to date follow the same pattern (QTD follows the calendar quarter)
Sales QTD =
IF (
    MIN ( 'Date'[Date] ) <= [Last Sales Date],
    TOTALQTD ( [Total Sales], 'Date'[Date] )
)

Sales MTD =
IF (
    MIN ( 'Date'[Date] ) <= [Last Sales Date],
    TOTALMTD ( [Total Sales], 'Date'[Date] )
)

-- Same period of the prior fiscal year
Sales FYTD PY =
CALCULATE ( [Sales FYTD], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( 'Date'[Date] ) )

Sales FYTD vs PY % =
VAR CurrentValue = [Sales FYTD]
VAR PriorValue   = [Sales FYTD PY]
RETURN
    IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( CurrentValue ) && NOT ISBLANK ( PriorValue ), DIVIDE ( CurrentValue - PriorValue, PriorValue ) )

-- Explicit version without TOTALYTD, handy when you need to add more filters
Sales FYTD (explicit) =
CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], DATESYTD ( 'Date'[Date], "6/30" ) )

-- Rolling 12 months ending on the last visible date
Sales Rolling 12M =
CALCULATE (
    [Total Sales],
    DATESINPERIOD ( 'Date'[Date], MAX ( 'Date'[Date] ), -12, MONTH )
)

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Change "6/30" to your fiscal year end; the string is read in the locale of the client where the model was created and the year part is ignored.
-- Replace [Total Sales] with any base measure (margin, quantity); all measures keep working.
-- Use the Fiscal Year column on slicers; on charts use Date[Date] or a month column on the axis.
-- To cut the lines at today instead of the last order, replace [Last Sales Date] by TODAY(); a dedicated 'data as of' value works too.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- Time intelligence needs a complete, contiguous Date table without gaps, marked as date table.
-- REMOVEFILTERS () inside CALCULATE is cheap; the value is a single aggregation, not an iteration over rows.
-- Keep the base measure simple (SUM); expensive base measures get multiplied by every derived measure.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Using a date column of the fact table in the time functions instead of the Date table column.
-- Hard-coding "12/31" and then wondering why the fiscal totals look like calendar totals.
-- Forgetting the guard: the YTD line continues flat for all future months otherwise.
-- Finding the last data date with ALL ( Sales ): filters coming from Date, Product or Customer still apply, so each cell gets its own last date; use REMOVEFILTERS ().
-- Mixing Fiscal Year on rows with calendar quarters; define fiscal quarter columns if you need them.

title: Year-over-year growth in DAX with like-for-like comparison of incomplete periods
summary: DAX measures for prior-year sales, absolute and percentage growth, and a like-for-like variant that compares only the days already available, avoiding the misleading drop in the current month.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- The simple YoY measure compares the current month with the whole prior-year month, which makes every running month
-- look like a decline. The like-for-like measure restricts both periods to the dates that have data, using variables
-- and SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR on a filtered date list. A measure for conditional formatting colours the result.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Sales[SalesAmount], Sales[OrderDate], Date[Date]. The Date table must be marked as date table.

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

Sales PY =
CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( 'Date'[Date] ) )

Sales YoY =
VAR CurrentValue = [Total Sales]
VAR PriorValue   = [Sales PY]
RETURN
    IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( CurrentValue ) && NOT ISBLANK ( PriorValue ), CurrentValue - PriorValue )

Sales YoY % =
DIVIDE ( [Total Sales] - [Sales PY], [Sales PY] )

-- Like-for-like: only dates up to the last day with data are used in BOTH years
Sales YoY % (like for like) =
VAR LastSalesDate = CALCULATE ( MAX ( Sales[OrderDate] ), REMOVEFILTERS () )
VAR VisibleDates =
    FILTER ( VALUES ( 'Date'[Date] ), 'Date'[Date] <= LastSalesDate )
VAR CurrentSales =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], VisibleDates )
VAR PriorSales =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( VisibleDates ) )
RETURN
    IF (
        NOT ISBLANK ( CurrentSales ) && NOT ISBLANK ( PriorSales ),
        DIVIDE ( CurrentSales - PriorSales, PriorSales )
    )

-- Alternative for month grain with DATEADD (works with months, quarters, years)
Sales PY (DATEADD) =
CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], DATEADD ( 'Date'[Date], -1, YEAR ) )

-- Same measure but using a different date relationship, for example shipping instead of ordering
-- (requires an inactive relationship Sales[ShipDate] -> Date[Date])
Sales PY by Ship Date =
CALCULATE (
    [Total Sales],
    USERELATIONSHIP ( Sales[ShipDate], 'Date'[Date] ),
    SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( 'Date'[Date] )
)

-- Conditional formatting helper: use as 'Field value' for font or background colour
YoY Colour =
VAR Growth = [Sales YoY % (like for like)]
RETURN
    SWITCH (
        TRUE (),
        ISBLANK ( Growth ), "#9E9E9E",
        Growth >= 0.10,     "#1B7F3B",
        Growth >= 0,        "#7FB77E",
        Growth > -0.10,     "#E39A3B",
        "#C0392B"
    )

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Set the format string of the percentage measures to 0.0% and of the absolute measure to #,0.
-- Swap SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR for DATEADD(..., -1, QUARTER) to compare with the previous quarter.
-- For a 52-week retail calendar use your own week index column and the pattern CALCULATE([Total Sales], FILTER(ALL('Date'), 'Date'[WeekIndex] = MAX('Date'[WeekIndex]) - 52)).
-- Replace Sales[ShipDate] with any second date column; relationship must exist and be inactive.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- The variables are evaluated once per cell; there is no hidden iteration over rows.
-- SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR over a filtered VALUES list is cheap, but avoid wrapping it inside iterators over customers.
-- Check results with Performance Analyzer; time-intelligence measures are mostly formula-engine work.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Dividing with the / operator: a missing prior year then returns Infinity or NaN; DIVIDE returns blank.
-- Comparing a partial current month with a full prior-year month and reading it as a decline.
-- Passing the fact-table date column to SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR; it needs the Date table column.
-- Using DATEADD with a month-end context and expecting day-exact results; it shifts the visible set of dates.

title: Moving averages in DAX: 3-month and 7-day windows that handle gaps correctly
summary: DAX measures for a trailing 3-month average of monthly sales and a 7-day or 90-day daily average, with a completeness check so the first periods do not show misleading values.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- Smooths volatile series with a trailing window. The monthly version averages the monthly totals of the last three months,
-- the daily version divides the window total by the number of days, so days without sales count as zero.
-- A completeness check suppresses values until the window is fully inside the data range.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Sales[SalesAmount], Sales[OrderDate], Date[Date], Date[YearMonth] (text such as 2025-03 with a sort-by column).

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

-- Trailing three months: average of the three monthly totals
Sales 3M Moving Avg =
VAR WindowDates =
    DATESINPERIOD ( 'Date'[Date], MAX ( 'Date'[Date] ), -3, MONTH )
VAR MonthsInWindow =
    CALCULATE ( DISTINCTCOUNT ( 'Date'[YearMonth] ), WindowDates )
VAR FirstDataDate =
    CALCULATE ( MIN ( Sales[OrderDate] ), REMOVEFILTERS () )
VAR WindowStart =
    MINX ( WindowDates, 'Date'[Date] )
RETURN
    -- only show values when the whole window lies inside the data range
    IF (
        MonthsInWindow = 3 && WindowStart >= FirstDataDate,
        CALCULATE (
            AVERAGEX ( VALUES ( 'Date'[YearMonth] ), [Total Sales] ),
            WindowDates
        )
    )

-- Trailing seven days; dividing by 7 treats days without sales as zero
Sales 7D Moving Avg =
VAR Window7 =
    DATESINPERIOD ( 'Date'[Date], MAX ( 'Date'[Date] ), -7, DAY )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], Window7 ), 7 )

-- Same idea with a parameter: window length chosen via a what-if table GENERATESERIES(7, 90, 1)
-- Calculated table:
Window Days =
GENERATESERIES ( 7, 90, 1 )

Window Days Value =
SELECTEDVALUE ( 'Window Days'[Value], 30 )

Sales N-Day Moving Avg =
VAR Days = [Window Days Value]
VAR WindowN =
    DATESINPERIOD ( 'Date'[Date], MAX ( 'Date'[Date] ), -Days, DAY )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], WindowN ), Days )

-- Comparison measure: distance of the current month from its own moving average
Sales vs 3M Avg % =
VAR AvgValue = [Sales 3M Moving Avg]
RETURN
    IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( AvgValue ), DIVIDE ( [Total Sales] - AvgValue, AvgValue ) )

-- Centred 3-month average (one month before, one after) for smoothing historical charts
Sales 3M Centred Avg =
VAR CurrentMonthEnd = MAX ( 'Date'[Date] )
VAR WindowDates =
    DATESBETWEEN (
        'Date'[Date],
        EOMONTH ( CurrentMonthEnd, -2 ) + 1,
        EOMONTH ( CurrentMonthEnd, 1 )
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE ( AVERAGEX ( VALUES ( 'Date'[YearMonth] ), [Total Sales] ), WindowDates )

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Change -3 and MONTH to -6 or -12 for longer windows; the completeness check needs the matching month count.
-- The 3-month measures expect a month-level axis; with a daily axis the window spans four calendar months and the check returns blank.
-- Use AVERAGEX over VALUES('Date'[Date]) instead of DIVIDE if blank days should be excluded from the average.
-- Add a slicer on 'Window Days'[Value] so report readers pick the smoothing length.
-- Plot the actual measure and the moving average in one line chart to show trend versus noise.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- DATESINPERIOD plus CALCULATE is evaluated per axis point; keep Date[Date] on the axis, not text columns.
-- VALUES('Date'[YearMonth]) inside AVERAGEX makes the iteration only as long as the window (3 rows).
-- Do not nest moving averages inside iterators over products; compute at the Date level and filter afterwards.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Averaging daily values with AVERAGEX when many days are blank: blank rows are skipped and inflate the average.
-- Showing the first two months of a 3-month average; they are based on fewer months and mislead.
-- Using a text month column without a sort-by column, so the axis order is alphabetical.
-- Forgetting to mark the Date table; the window then may not clear filters of Year and Month columns.

title: Top N with an 'Other' bucket in DAX using a disconnected axis table
summary: Shows the top N products by sales plus one 'Other' bar for the remainder, with N chosen by a slicer, built from a disconnected helper table and TOPN with EXCEPT, so the total always adds up.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- A plain Top N visual filter drops the rest of the data and the total no longer matches. This pattern builds an axis table
-- with all product names plus the entry 'Other'. A single measure returns the product's sales when it is in the top N,
-- the sum of all remaining products for 'Other' and blank for everyone else. A what-if slicer controls N.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Product[ProductName], Sales[SalesAmount]. Two helper tables are created (no relationships to them):
--   'Top N Axis' (column Item) and 'Top N Parameter' (GENERATESERIES).

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

-- Helper table 1: the axis, all products plus the synthetic member "Other" (no relationships!)
Top N Axis =
UNION (
    SELECTCOLUMNS ( ALL ( Product[ProductName] ), "Item", Product[ProductName] ),
    ROW ( "Item", "Other" )
)

-- Helper table 2: the choice of N for a slicer (column is named [Value])
Top N Parameter =
GENERATESERIES ( 3, 20, 1 )

Top N Value =
SELECTEDVALUE ( 'Top N Parameter'[Value], 5 )

-- The measure used in the visual. Axis = 'Top N Axis'[Item], Values = [Top N Sales]
Top N Sales =
VAR N    = [Top N Value]
VAR Item = SELECTEDVALUE ( 'Top N Axis'[Item] )
-- all products visible under slicers, regardless of the row of the visual
VAR VisibleProducts = ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] )
VAR TopProducts =
    TOPN ( N, VisibleProducts, [Total Sales], DESC )
RETURN
    SWITCH (
        TRUE (),
        -- total row: the item axis has several values, return the real total
        ISBLANK ( Item ), [Total Sales],
        -- everything that is not in the top N
        Item = "Other",
            CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], EXCEPT ( VisibleProducts, TopProducts ) ),
        -- an item in the top N shows its own sales, anything else stays blank
        CONTAINS ( TopProducts, Product[ProductName], Item ),
            CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], Product[ProductName] = Item )
    )

-- Share of the grand total, useful as a second value or data label
Top N Share % =
DIVIDE ( [Top N Sales], CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED () ) )

-- Sort helper: items by sales descending with "Other" always last; use it as sort measure in a table visual
Top N Sort =
VAR Item = SELECTEDVALUE ( 'Top N Axis'[Item] )
RETURN
    IF ( Item = "Other", -1, [Top N Sales] )

-- Label for the chart title that reacts to the slicer
Top N Title =
"Top " & [Top N Value] & " products by sales, remaining products grouped as Other"

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Replace Product[ProductName] by Customer[CustomerName] or Product[Subcategory]; adjust the axis table likewise.
-- Change the ranking measure inside TOPN (for example [Total Margin]) to rank by another metric.
-- Set a visual-level filter 'Top N Sales is not blank' on the visual and sort descending by Top N Sales.
-- Add a second 'Other' threshold such as a minimum share by wrapping the TOPN table in FILTER.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- TOPN is evaluated once per visual cell; with many thousand items it becomes the expensive step.
-- Pre-aggregate on a dimension with fewer members (Subcategory) if the ranking runs over a huge product list.
-- Keep the axis table small and without relationships; it should not filter any fact table.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Using a visual-level Top N filter: it hides the rest and the total no longer reconciles.
-- Creating a relationship between 'Top N Axis' and Product; the pattern relies on there being none.
-- Forgetting that ties at position N can return more than N items; add a tie-breaker column if that matters.
-- Sorting the axis alphabetically, so 'Other' lands in the middle; sort by the measure instead.

title: Pareto analysis and ABC classification of products in DAX
summary: Calculates each product's cumulative share of sales with tie-breaking, classifies products into A, B and C by 80 and 95 percent thresholds, and counts products and sales per class.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- Pareto charts show how few products create most of the revenue. The cumulative share of a product is the sum of the sales
-- of all products that sell at least as much, divided by the total. ABC classes build on that: A up to 80 percent,
-- B up to 95 percent, C the long tail. The measures respect slicers because they use ALLSELECTED.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Product[ProductName], Sales[SalesAmount]. Works on any other dimension column by exchanging the column name.

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

-- Thresholds as measures so that they can be changed in one place
ABC Threshold A = 0.80
ABC Threshold B = 0.95

Sales Share of Selection =
DIVIDE ( [Total Sales], CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ) ) )

-- Cumulative share: add up all products ranked before or equal to the current one
Pareto Cumulative Share =
VAR CurrentSales = [Total Sales]
VAR CurrentName  = SELECTEDVALUE ( Product[ProductName] )
VAR GrandTotal =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ) )
VAR Peers =
    FILTER ( ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ), [Total Sales] > 0 )
VAR CumulativeSales =
    SUMX (
        FILTER (
            Peers,
            -- the second condition is a tie-breaker so equal products do not both claim the same position
            [Total Sales] > CurrentSales
                || ( [Total Sales] = CurrentSales && Product[ProductName] <= CurrentName )
        ),
        [Total Sales]
    )
RETURN
    IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( CurrentSales ), DIVIDE ( CumulativeSales, GrandTotal ) )

-- ABC class: a product is A if it STARTED below the threshold (so the product that crosses 80 percent is still A)
ABC Class =
VAR Cumulative = [Pareto Cumulative Share]
VAR StartShare = Cumulative - [Sales Share of Selection]
RETURN
    IF (
        NOT ISBLANK ( Cumulative ),
        SWITCH (
            TRUE (),
            StartShare < [ABC Threshold A], "A",
            StartShare < [ABC Threshold B], "B",
            "C"
        )
    )

-- Number of products per class (use with the class on rows, or filter in a card)
Products in Class A =
COUNTROWS (
    FILTER ( ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ), [ABC Class] = "A" )
)

-- Sales of the A items and their contribution to total sales
Sales of Class A =
SUMX (
    FILTER ( ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ), [ABC Class] = "A" ),
    [Total Sales]
)

Class A Sales Share =
DIVIDE ( [Sales of Class A], CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ) ) )

-- Pareto rank for the x axis ordering (1 = best seller)
Pareto Rank =
IF (
    NOT ISBLANK ( [Total Sales] ),
    RANKX ( ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ), [Total Sales], , DESC, DENSE )
)

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- For customers use Customer[CustomerName]; for categories use Product[Category]. Replace in all measures.
-- Move the thresholds to a what-if parameter table to let users test 70/90 or 80/95.
-- Build the Pareto chart as clustered column (Total Sales) plus line (Pareto Cumulative Share) sorted by sales.
-- Use [ABC Class] as legend or conditional-format value in a table of products.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- The cumulative measure is O(n squared): for each product it scans all peers. Fine for a few thousand, slow for 100k.
-- For big dimensions pre-compute the class in Power Query or as a calculated column on a summary table.
-- Filter out products without sales early (the Peers variable) to keep the iteration short.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Using ALL instead of ALLSELECTED: then slicers are ignored and the shares do not add up to 100 percent in the visual.
-- Dropping the tie-breaker; products with identical sales then show the same cumulative share, which flattens the curve and can misplace the A/B/C borders.
-- Classifying by cumulative share alone: the product that crosses the threshold would land in class B.
-- Reading class A as 'best 20 percent of products'; it is defined by sales share, not by item count.

title: Customer cohort retention matrix in DAX (first purchase month)
summary: Builds a cohort retention matrix: customers grouped by first purchase month, with the share still buying 0 to 12 months later, based on a calculated column, a disconnected offset table and one measure.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- A cohort is the group of customers whose first order happened in the same month. The matrix shows for each cohort how many of
-- those customers ordered again 1, 2, ... 12 months later. Rows are cohort months, columns are the month offset, cells are
-- retention percentages. Revenue cohorts use the same structure with [Total Sales] instead of the distinct customer count.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Customer[CustomerKey], Sales[CustomerKey], Sales[OrderDate], Sales[SalesAmount], Date[Date].
-- Helper table: 'Cohort Offset' (0 to 12), no relationship.

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
-- ---- Calculated columns on the Customer table --------------------------------
-- Context transition turns the current customer row into a filter on Sales
First Purchase Date =
CALCULATE ( MIN ( Sales[OrderDate] ) )

Cohort Month =
IF (
    NOT ISBLANK ( Customer[First Purchase Date] ),
    DATE ( YEAR ( Customer[First Purchase Date] ), MONTH ( Customer[First Purchase Date] ), 1 )
)

-- ---- Calculated table (no relationships) -----------------------------------------
Cohort Offset =
GENERATESERIES ( 0, 12, 1 )

-- ---- Measures ----------------------------------------------------------------
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

Cohort Size =
CALCULATE ( COUNTROWS ( Customer ), REMOVEFILTERS ( 'Cohort Offset' ) )

-- Customers of the selected cohort that bought in the month (cohort month + offset)
Cohort Active Customers =
VAR OffsetValue      = SELECTEDVALUE ( 'Cohort Offset'[Value] )
VAR CohortMonth = SELECTEDVALUE ( Customer[Cohort Month] )
VAR TargetStart = EDATE ( CohortMonth, OffsetValue )
-- first day of the following month: an upper bound that also keeps orders with a time part on the last day
VAR TargetNext  = EDATE ( CohortMonth, OffsetValue + 1 )
VAR LastOrder   = CALCULATE ( MAX ( Sales[OrderDate] ), REMOVEFILTERS () )
RETURN
    IF (
        NOT ISBLANK ( OffsetValue ) && NOT ISBLANK ( CohortMonth ) && TargetStart <= LastOrder,
        CALCULATE (
            DISTINCTCOUNT ( Sales[CustomerKey] ),
            -- date slicers must not shrink the observation month
            REMOVEFILTERS ( 'Date' ),
            Sales[OrderDate] >= TargetStart,
            Sales[OrderDate] < TargetNext
        )
    )

Cohort Retention % =
DIVIDE ( [Cohort Active Customers], [Cohort Size] )

-- Same matrix for revenue: how much did each cohort spend in month N
Cohort Revenue =
VAR OffsetValue      = SELECTEDVALUE ( 'Cohort Offset'[Value] )
VAR CohortMonth = SELECTEDVALUE ( Customer[Cohort Month] )
VAR TargetStart = EDATE ( CohortMonth, OffsetValue )
-- first day of the following month: an upper bound that also keeps orders with a time part on the last day
VAR TargetNext  = EDATE ( CohortMonth, OffsetValue + 1 )
RETURN
    IF (
        NOT ISBLANK ( OffsetValue ) && NOT ISBLANK ( CohortMonth ),
        CALCULATE (
            [Total Sales],
            REMOVEFILTERS ( 'Date' ),
            Sales[OrderDate] >= TargetStart,
            Sales[OrderDate] < TargetNext
        )
    )

-- Average retention across the visible cohorts (bottom row of the matrix)
Avg Retention % =
AVERAGEX ( VALUES ( Customer[Cohort Month] ), [Cohort Retention %] )

-- Visual setup: Matrix, rows = Customer[Cohort Month] (format mmm yyyy),
-- columns = 'Cohort Offset'[Value], values = [Cohort Retention %]; add a colour scale as conditional format.

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Use Customer[Country] or a segment as an additional slicer to compare cohorts of different markets.
-- Switch to week cohorts with a week start column and 'Cohort Offset' counted in weeks (DATEADD with WEEK is not available, use +7*offset).
-- Exclude refunds by adding a filter on Sales[SalesAmount] > 0 inside the CALCULATE statements.
-- Limit the cohort history with a slicer on Customer[Cohort Month] to the last 12 to 24 months.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- The calculated columns are computed at refresh time (once per customer); the measure itself is cheap per cell.
-- DISTINCTCOUNT on Sales[CustomerKey] is fast in the VertiPaq engine, but only when Sales is not a DirectQuery source.
-- For very large customer tables compute First Purchase Date in Power Query or the source to speed up refresh.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Defining First Purchase Date as a measure; a column is required to group customers by cohort in the matrix.
-- Relating 'Cohort Offset' to another table; it has to stay disconnected.
-- Counting future months as zero retention; the guard against LastOrder returns blank instead.
-- Letting a date slicer filter the observation month, which removes returning customers from the numerator.

title: Semi-additive measures in DAX: closing, opening and average balance for inventory snapshots
summary: DAX measures for snapshot data such as stock or account balances that must not be summed over time: closing and opening balance, per-product correctness for missing snapshots, average and net change.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- Inventory levels or bank balances can be summed across products but not across dates. A month total is the value of the last
-- snapshot in that month, not the sum of 30 daily values. The measures here pick the last available snapshot (even if the
-- month end is missing), the previous snapshot as opening balance, and calculate average and change in the period.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Inventory (snapshot fact: SnapshotDate, ProductKey, UnitsOnHand) with relationships to Date[Date] (via SnapshotDate) and Product[ProductKey].
-- Product[UnitCost] is used only by the stock value measure.

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
-- Wrong: summing balances over a period gives a meaningless number
Units On Hand (sum, do not use) =
SUM ( Inventory[UnitsOnHand] )

-- Closing balance, option 1: LASTNONBLANK on the date column.
-- The date expression counts snapshot rows, so days without a snapshot are skipped.
Closing Units =
CALCULATE (
    SUM ( Inventory[UnitsOnHand] ),
    LASTNONBLANK ( 'Date'[Date], CALCULATE ( COUNTROWS ( Inventory ) ) )
)

-- Closing balance, option 2: pick the last snapshot date explicitly (easier to debug)
Closing Units (explicit) =
VAR LastSnapshot = MAX ( Inventory[SnapshotDate] )
RETURN
    CALCULATE ( SUM ( Inventory[UnitsOnHand] ), Inventory[SnapshotDate] = LastSnapshot )

-- Per-product correct: each product uses ITS OWN last snapshot in the period
Closing Units (per product) =
SUMX (
    VALUES ( Product[ProductKey] ),
    CALCULATE (
        SUM ( Inventory[UnitsOnHand] ),
        LASTNONBLANK ( 'Date'[Date], CALCULATE ( COUNTROWS ( Inventory ) ) )
    )
)

-- Opening balance: the last snapshot BEFORE the first visible date
Opening Units =
VAR PeriodStart = MIN ( 'Date'[Date] )
VAR PreviousSnapshot =
    CALCULATE (
        MAX ( Inventory[SnapshotDate] ),
        FILTER ( ALL ( 'Date' ), 'Date'[Date] < PeriodStart )
    )
RETURN
    CALCULATE (
        SUM ( Inventory[UnitsOnHand] ),
        REMOVEFILTERS ( 'Date' ),
        Inventory[SnapshotDate] = PreviousSnapshot
    )

Net Change Units =
VAR Opening = [Opening Units]
VAR Closing = [Closing Units (explicit)]
RETURN
    IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( Closing ), Closing - COALESCE ( Opening, 0 ) )

-- Average stock level: average of the daily totals over days that have a snapshot
Average Units On Hand =
AVERAGEX (
    VALUES ( 'Date'[Date] ),
    CALCULATE ( SUM ( Inventory[UnitsOnHand] ) )
)

-- Month end value of the same metric, e.g. for a monthly column chart
Closing Units Month End =
CALCULATE ( [Closing Units], DATESMTD ( LASTDATE ( 'Date'[Date] ) ) )

-- Stock value: balance x cost, still semi-additive
Closing Stock Value =
VAR LastSnapshot = MAX ( Inventory[SnapshotDate] )
RETURN
    SUMX (
        CALCULATETABLE ( Inventory, Inventory[SnapshotDate] = LastSnapshot ),
        Inventory[UnitsOnHand] * RELATED ( Product[UnitCost] )
    )

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Rename the measures and columns to your balance table (account balances, headcount, open tickets, backlog).
-- Use Closing Units (per product) when snapshots are irregular per product; otherwise option 1 is faster.
-- Product[UnitCost] must exist in the Product table for the stock value; replace with your cost column.
-- For DirectQuery sources prefer the explicit variant, it translates into simpler SQL.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- LASTNONBLANK evaluates its expression for each date in the context; wide date ranges with many snapshots cost more.
-- The per-product version iterates over all visible products: use it for detail tables, not for company-wide cards.
-- Keep snapshots in a narrow fact table (date, key, value) and avoid a calculated column per row.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Summing the balance over time and then dividing by the number of days to 'fix' it.
-- Using LASTDATE: it returns the last date in the period even when no snapshot exists, leading to blank results.
-- Taking the global last snapshot when products have different last dates; use the per-product measure.
-- Applying the opening balance logic to the first month of the data; it is blank because no earlier snapshot exists.

title: Running total in DAX: cumulative sales over time, per year and as percent of total
summary: DAX measures for a cumulative running total across the selected period, one that resets every year, a cumulative percentage of the total and a version that stops at the last day with data.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- Running totals add the value of every previous period to the current one. The core pattern is CALCULATE with a filter on the date
-- column from the first to the current visible date. Variants reset at each year, work on a month index and stop at the last
-- data date, so the line does not stay flat in the future.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Sales[SalesAmount], Sales[Quantity], Sales[OrderDate], Date[Date], Date[Year], Date[YearMonth], Date[MonthIndex] (integer, one per month).

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

Total Quantity =
SUM ( Sales[Quantity] )

-- Classic running total across all dates that are visible in the report (respects slicers on Date)
Running Total Sales =
VAR LastVisibleDate = MAX ( 'Date'[Date] )
RETURN
    CALCULATE (
        [Total Sales],
        FILTER ( ALLSELECTED ( 'Date' ), 'Date'[Date] <= LastVisibleDate )
    )

-- Same, but blank after the last day with data so the line ends where the data ends
Running Total Sales (to last sale) =
VAR LastSalesDate = CALCULATE ( MAX ( Sales[OrderDate] ), REMOVEFILTERS () )
VAR LastVisibleDate = MAX ( 'Date'[Date] )
RETURN
    IF (
        LastVisibleDate <= LastSalesDate,
        CALCULATE (
            [Total Sales],
            FILTER ( ALLSELECTED ( 'Date' ), 'Date'[Date] <= LastVisibleDate )
        )
    )

-- Resets every year: running total inside the calendar year
Running Total Sales (YTD) =
CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], DATESYTD ( 'Date'[Date] ) )

-- Month-grain running total using an integer month index; works when the axis is a month text column
Running Total Sales (by month index) =
VAR CurrentIndex = MAX ( 'Date'[MonthIndex] )
RETURN
    CALCULATE (
        [Total Sales],
        FILTER ( ALLSELECTED ( 'Date' ), 'Date'[MonthIndex] <= CurrentIndex )
    )

-- Cumulative percentage of the total shown on the visual (for a cumulative curve)
Running Total % =
VAR GrandTotal =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( 'Date' ) )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( [Running Total Sales], GrandTotal )

-- Cumulative quantity with the same pattern
Running Total Quantity =
VAR LastVisibleDate = MAX ( 'Date'[Date] )
RETURN
    CALCULATE (
        [Total Quantity],
        FILTER ( ALLSELECTED ( 'Date' ), 'Date'[Date] <= LastVisibleDate )
    )

-- Running total against a target: remaining gap to a yearly goal (goal = what-if or fixed number)
Sales Target Year = 1200000

Gap to Target =
VAR Gap = [Sales Target Year] - [Running Total Sales (YTD)]
RETURN
    IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( [Running Total Sales (YTD)] ), MAX ( Gap, 0 ) )

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Replace [Total Sales] by any additive measure (cost, margin, tickets).
-- To reset by fiscal year, use DATESYTD ( 'Date'[Date], "6/30" ) or a fiscal year column and ALLSELECTED on it.
-- To get a running total over a non-date dimension (such as products sorted by sales), use the Pareto pattern with a rank column.
-- The newer window functions (WINDOW, OFFSET) can express the same logic; the CALCULATE version works in every model.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- FILTER over ALLSELECTED('Date') is evaluated per axis point; a daily axis over ten years is slow, use months.
-- A month-index based running total does a smaller scan than a daily one; prefer it for monthly charts.
-- Avoid calling the running total inside another iterator, the cost multiplies.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Using ALL instead of ALLSELECTED: the running total then ignores slicers and starts at the beginning of the Date table.
-- Using MAX('Date'[Date]) with a month column on the axis and forgetting that the month's last day is used, which is correct only for full months.
-- Letting the Date table run beyond the data: without the guard the line stays flat in the future.
-- Expecting the total row of the visual to show the last value; it shows the running value at the last visible date.

title: Dynamic ranking in DAX: RANKX within category, tie-breaking and rank change versus last year
summary: Measures that rank products overall and inside each category with RANKX, produce unique ranks by tie-breaker, flag the top 3 per group and show the movement in rank against the prior year.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- RANKX over a whole dimension ignores the row grouping in a matrix, so ranks run across categories. The pattern here builds
-- the peer set with ALLSELECTED over name and category and filters it to the current category. Dense ranks, unique ranks with
-- a deterministic tie-breaker and the rank movement versus the same period last year are included.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Product[ProductName], Product[Category], Sales[SalesAmount], Date[Date]. The measures work in a table or matrix with products on rows.

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

-- Overall rank among all products that are visible under the current slicers
Product Rank Overall =
IF (
    ISINSCOPE ( Product[ProductName] ) && NOT ISBLANK ( [Total Sales] ),
    RANKX ( ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ), [Total Sales], , DESC, DENSE )
)

-- Rank inside the category of the current row
Product Rank in Category =
VAR CurrentCategory = SELECTEDVALUE ( Product[Category] )
VAR Peers =
    FILTER (
        ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName], Product[Category] ),
        Product[Category] = CurrentCategory
    )
RETURN
    IF (
        ISINSCOPE ( Product[ProductName] ) && NOT ISBLANK ( [Total Sales] ) && NOT ISBLANK ( CurrentCategory ),
        RANKX ( Peers, [Total Sales], , DESC, DENSE )
    )

-- Unique rank: ties are resolved alphabetically so that positions are 1, 2, 3, 4 without repetition
Unique Rank in Category =
VAR CurrentSales    = [Total Sales]
VAR CurrentName     = SELECTEDVALUE ( Product[ProductName] )
VAR CurrentCategory = SELECTEDVALUE ( Product[Category] )
VAR Peers =
    FILTER (
        ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName], Product[Category] ),
        Product[Category] = CurrentCategory
    )
RETURN
    IF (
        ISINSCOPE ( Product[ProductName] ) && NOT ISBLANK ( CurrentSales ) && NOT ISBLANK ( CurrentCategory ),
        COUNTROWS (
            FILTER (
                Peers,
                [Total Sales] > CurrentSales
                    || ( [Total Sales] = CurrentSales && Product[ProductName] < CurrentName )
            )
        ) + 1
    )

-- Sales of the best three products per category, blank for the others (use in a stacked chart)
Sales of Top 3 in Category =
VAR RankValue = [Unique Rank in Category]
RETURN
    -- a blank rank must not pass the test: BLANK <= 3 is TRUE in DAX
    IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( RankValue ) && RankValue <= 3, [Total Sales] )

-- Rank in the same period of the prior year
Product Rank in Category PY =
CALCULATE ( [Product Rank in Category], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR ( 'Date'[Date] ) )

-- Positive number = moved up. Format as +0;-0;0 with up/down arrows via conditional icons
Rank Movement =
VAR RankNow = [Product Rank in Category]
VAR RankBefore = [Product Rank in Category PY]
RETURN
    IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( RankNow ) && NOT ISBLANK ( RankBefore ), RankBefore - RankNow )

-- Text label for tooltips, e.g. "#2 in Bikes (was #5)"
Rank Label =
VAR RankNow = [Product Rank in Category]
VAR RankBefore = [Product Rank in Category PY]
RETURN
    IF (
        NOT ISBLANK ( RankNow ),
        "#" & RankNow & " in " & SELECTEDVALUE ( Product[Category] )
            & IF ( NOT ISBLANK ( RankBefore ), " (was #" & RankBefore & ")", " (new)" )
    )

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Replace Product[Category] with Product[Brand] or Customer[Country] to rank inside another group.
-- Use SKIP instead of DENSE in RANKX if ties should leave gaps (1, 2, 2, 4).
-- Rank by another metric by changing the second argument, for example [Total Margin] or [Customer Count].
-- To rank only visible top items in a card use TOPN ( 3, Peers, [Total Sales] ) and concatenate with CONCATENATEX.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- RANKX evaluates the measure once per peer; the cost is peers x cells, keep the peer set restricted to the group.
-- Compute rank movement only in detail visuals; in a visual with thousands of rows it doubles the work.
-- Prefer ALLSELECTED over ALL so slicers and cross-filtering shrink the peer set automatically.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Ranking over ALLSELECTED(Product[ProductName]) in a matrix grouped by category and wondering why ranks do not restart.
-- Not handling blanks: RANKX then ranks products without sales at the bottom instead of leaving them empty.
-- Using the rank as a sort key without a tie-breaker; the visual order of tied rows changes between refreshes.
-- Showing a rank in a total or subtotal row, where it would rank a total against single products; the ISINSCOPE guards return blank there.

title: Percent of total, percent of parent and percent of year measures in DAX
summary: Share-of-total measures that respect slicers: percent of visible grand total, a hierarchy-aware percent of parent using ISINSCOPE, percent of year and column percent for segments, with correct total rows.
body:
-- ==== What it does ====
-- Percentages of a total are among the most requested measures and the most often wrong in total rows. The measures here
-- use ALLSELECTED so slicers are respected, ISINSCOPE to detect the level of a matrix hierarchy and variables for readability.
-- Each measure keeps the denominator logic explicit so that the numbers can be audited against a pivot table.

-- ==== Required tables/columns ====
-- Model assumed: a generic star schema. Sales (fact: OrderID, OrderDate, CustomerKey, ProductKey, Quantity, UnitPrice, UnitCost, SalesAmount),
--   Date (Date, Year, Quarter, MonthNumber, MonthName, YearMonth), Customer (CustomerKey, CustomerName, Country, Segment),
--   Product (ProductKey, ProductName, Category, Subcategory, Brand). One-to-many relationships from the dimensions to Sales,
--   Sales[OrderDate] to Date[Date] is the active date relationship, and Date is marked as the date table.
-- Sales[SalesAmount], Product[Category], Product[Subcategory], Product[ProductName], Customer[Segment], Date[Year], Date[MonthNumber].

-- ==== Code ====
-- Each block is one measure (or calculated column/table) created with New measure / New column / New table.
Total Sales =
SUM ( Sales[SalesAmount] )

-- Percent of the grand total of everything visible in the visual (slicers apply, rows and columns do not)
Pct of Visible Total =
DIVIDE ( [Total Sales], CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED () ) )

-- Percent of parent for a matrix with Category > Subcategory > ProductName on rows.
-- ISINSCOPE tells at which level the current cell is; the denominator removes only the filter of that level.
Pct of Parent =
VAR Numerator = [Total Sales]
VAR Denominator =
    SWITCH (
        TRUE (),
        ISINSCOPE ( Product[ProductName] ),
            CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( Product[ProductName] ) ),
        ISINSCOPE ( Product[Subcategory] ),
            CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( Product[Subcategory] ) ),
        ISINSCOPE ( Product[Category] ),
            CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLSELECTED ( Product[Category] ) ),
        -- grand total row
        Numerator
    )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( Numerator, Denominator )

-- Percent of the year total in a matrix with months on rows (resets in every year)
Pct of Year =
VAR YearTotal =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], ALLEXCEPT ( 'Date', 'Date'[Year] ) )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( [Total Sales], YearTotal )

-- Column percent: share of a customer segment within the product on rows
Pct of Product by Segment =
VAR ProductTotal =
    CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS ( Customer[Segment] ) )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( [Total Sales], ProductTotal )

-- Share of the selected item compared with all other items of the same column (for cards)
Selected Category Share =
VAR SelectedSales = [Total Sales]
VAR AllSales = CALCULATE ( [Total Sales], REMOVEFILTERS ( Product[Category] ) )
RETURN
    DIVIDE ( SelectedSales, AllSales )

-- Helper to prove that the shares add up (should return 100 percent in every total row)
Pct Check =
SUMX ( VALUES ( Product[Category] ), [Pct of Visible Total] )

-- Data label text combining value and share, e.g. "125,400 (12.4%)"
Sales with Share =
VAR Share = [Pct of Visible Total]
RETURN
    FORMAT ( [Total Sales], "#,0" ) & " (" & FORMAT ( Share, "0.0%" ) & ")"

-- ==== How to adapt ====
-- Set the format of the percentage measures to 0.0 %; the label measure formats on its own.
-- Swap ALLSELECTED for ALL when the share must be computed against everything regardless of slicers (market share view).
-- Add more ISINSCOPE branches for deeper hierarchies; list the deepest level first.
-- Replace Customer[Segment] by Customer[Country] for a country mix per product.

-- ==== Performance notes ====
-- ALLSELECTED() without arguments depends on the visual's shadow filter context and can be expensive on wide matrices.
-- Prefer the column-specific form ALLSELECTED ( Product[Category] ) when only one level is needed.
-- DIVIDE avoids division-by-zero errors and costs nothing compared with an IF check.

-- ==== Common mistakes ====
-- Using ALL instead of ALLSELECTED: shares then ignore slicers and no longer add up to 100 percent in the visual.
-- Testing the shallow level first in SWITCH: ISINSCOPE ( Category ) is also true on subcategory and product rows, so the deepest level must come first.
-- Using ALLEXCEPT on a table that has slicers; it removes the slicer filters on that whole table.
-- Formatting percentages with FORMAT in the main measure; the result becomes text and cannot be summed or charted.
